page.layout: One page of running text, no margin notes. Running head "IURIS." with page number "501" at the top. Below the head, a short question and answer in roman and italic, then a horizontal ornamental rule. Then a title block: a question heading, the title with a black-letter German addition, two italic questions, and their answer paragraphs. Signature "I 3" at the lower right.

l.i: EST jus, quo liberi ad bona matrum intestatarum

main_text.l: Sciendum est etiam illos liberos, qui vulgò

l.i: Ad quos pertinet hæreditas suis & agnatis

main_text.l: Post suos hæredes, eosq; quos inter suos hære-
des prætor & constitutiones vocant, & post legi-
timos, quo numero sunt agnati, & hi, quos in locum
nostra erexit constitutio, proximos cognatos prætor

l.i: Ad quos secundò pertinet hæreditas suis & agna-

main_text.l: Eos etiam, qui per fœminini sexus personas ex
transverso cognatione junguntur, tertio gradu pro-
ximitatis nomine prætor ad successionem vocat.§.

page.notes: The running head is set in small capitals: "IVRIS" in print, transcribed as IURIS. The page number is printed in old-style figures ("5oı"), transcribed as 501. The ornamental rule between the two sections is not text and is omitted. The drop caps E and P are joined to the following word. "Vocantúrne" and "cùm" keep their printed accents. The black-letter phrase "von gemeinen weibern gebo:en" is read as "geboren"; the final letter is a little unclear, so please check it. "Bon er-" in the title is most likely black-letter "Von", as the rest of the German phrase suggests. The first line of the title, "De successione cognatorum, Von er-", ends with a printed hyphen that carries over to "bung". The question "Quid dicis de vulgò quæsitis?" has its initial Q underlined in print. The question lines are italic and set apart, so they are treated as level-2 headings. The long-s "fi" ligature in "fiimilitudinem" is transcribed as "similitudinem".
